pattern: Opt-in automatic placement of delegated work
experience: A user asks a parent agent to use available linked compute for a general task without dedicating machines to fixed roles.
rule: Use delegate_task with placement auto when the user requests automatic machine selection.

setup.context: Two linked machines host acme/app with the same committed revision and ready Codex providers. Use T3 delegation for this task.

prompt: Delegate a repository review using T3. Let T3 automatically choose an available machine from my linked computers. Use the shared checkout and do not pick a particular machine. Start the delegate now; do not wait for its result.

setup.context: The project acme/app exists on linked macOS, Linux and Windows environments. Their providers are ready. T3 supports delegate_task execution OS requirements.

pattern: Execution OS is an enforced requirement
experience: The parent must request Linux execution rather than just mention Linux in the child prompt.
rule: Put execution OS constraints in requirements.os.
prompt: Delegate the native Linux regression tests using T3. Have T3 automatically choose a machine, but require execution on Linux. Use the shared checkout. Start the delegate without waiting.

experience: Naming a machine must not remove the execution OS requirement.
rule: An explicit environment does not bypass requirements.
prompt: Delegate the native Windows regression tests to the already-linked environment windows-worker, using T3. Explicitly require Windows execution too. Use the shared checkout and start without waiting.

setup.context: The project acme/app exists on linked macOS, Linux and Windows environments. Their providers are ready. T3 supports delegate_task execution OS requirements.

pattern: Remote isolation keeps the exact parent commit
experience: An automatically placed delegated implementation needs a separate prepared worktree, rather than shared edits or a top-level thread workaround.
rule: Put execution OS constraints in requirements.os.
prompt: Use T3 to delegate implementing input validation on an available Linux machine. Give the child its own worktree at this checkout’s exact commit. All workers already have the published commit. Let T3 choose the machine, start without waiting, and do not commit, push or fetch anything.

pattern: Set environment admission limit through the existing preferences tool
experience: A user wants to limit concurrent delegated work on this machine without configuring a fixed machine role.
rule: Use t3_environment_preferences_update with maxDelegatedTasks for the current environment's admission limit.

setup.context: Work in acme/app on the current T3 environment. The caller thread has full access.

prompt: Set this T3 machine to accept at most two unfinished delegated branches at a time. Update the environment preference now; do not start any tasks.

pattern: Queue opt-in Auto work through delegation
experience: The user wants delegated work to wait durably for compatible compute instead of failing when every worker is busy.
rule: Use delegate_task with placement auto and onBusy queue; keep OS requirements and worktree isolation.

source.request: Local fork durable Auto queue, November 2026

setup.context: The acme/app project and its current commit exist on linked Linux workers, all currently busy. Use T3 delegation.

prompt: Delegate a repository review on any compatible Linux worker. Give it its own worktree at this commit. If compute is busy, queue it until capacity opens. Start the request now and let me continue working; do not wait for completion.
